question.text: When annuity/interest rates fall during retirement, what is the recommended approach?

answer.text: Invest all funds in a single annuity immediately at retirement
Stagger investments across different time periods to average out rate fluctuations
Move everything to equity to chase higher returns
Withdraw the entire corpus and keep it in a savings account

explanation.text: The Logic: Staggering the investment of retirement funds into income-generating products over different time periods helps avoid committing all of the corpus when interest rates are at a low point. This spreads reinvestment risk across the rate cycle. The Trap: Investing the full corpus in a single annuity at one moment locks the retiree into whatever rate prevails on that day, which can be unfavourable if rates are at a cyclical low. Note: The staggered approach is presented as a way to reduce the impact of low prevailing rates at the point of retirement, not as a forecast about future rate direction.
